td-3-103.title: Across the Glass Ledge
td-3-103.text: Frost-slicked windowpanes offer a narrow footing suspended high above the echoing darkness of the primary water reservoir. Below, the dark liquid laps silently against iron pillars while far overhead salt-crusted girders groan in the cold draught. A discarded leather toolbelt hangs precariously from a protruding rivet on the opposite pier, swaying gently with every gust that whistles through the stilt-city struts. Balance requires absolute focus as boots find only inches of smooth, condensation-filmed plate glass.
exits: Step across to the dangling leather

td-3-104.title: Glass Above The Sump
td-3-104.text: Salt-crusted brine laps against the vertical walls of the reservoir far below, a grey eye staring upward through forty feet of dead air. The suspended walkway consists of thick panes bolted directly into iron ribs, their upper surfaces pitted white from decades of chemical condensation. A drowned worker's heavy leather toolbelt hangs snagged upon an external bracing strut, just beyond a rusted railing missing three vertical bars. You ease your boots onto the translucent glass, feeling the cold surface bow slightly under your weight while the distant drip of moisture echoes endlessly in the hollow shaft.
exits: Slip back into the rotting archives

td-3-105.title: Slip on the Pane
td-3-105.text: A sudden tremor in the stilt-work sends the boots skidding across the condensation-slicked glass before purchase can be found. Arms windmill wildly against the void, catching hard against a rusted iron bracket that leaves a deep, stinging purple bruise across the forearm. The heavy belt slides off the far rivet and drops silently into the deep water below, leaving only bruised ribs and a bitter taste of rust in the mouth. Shivering and breathless, the foothold is finally secured on the far platform.

td-3-106.title: The Glass Ledge
td-3-106.text: Your boots slide with a sickening screech against the curved pane, suspended high above the echoing vault of the reservoir. Down in the dark, black water laps against lead walls, waiting for anyone foolish enough to lose their footing. Every breath is a struggle against the damp chill rising from the depths, yet your trembling fingers finally close around the heavy leather straps of the drowned worker's toolbelt. Hauling it up onto solid stone, you secure a grease-stained brass wedge - a simple keepsake that might just jam a lock when the time is right.
exits: Slip back into the dusty annex

td-3-107.title: The Governors Ink
td-3-107.text: Heavy iron-bound ledgers lie scattered across the mahogany table of the inner chamber, bearing the neat, ruthless script of the Brineholder magistracy. Parchment maps pinned to the cedar walls reveal that the great pumping engine at the foot of the Sunken Stair has not merely jammed by accident, but has been deliberately welded shut by royal decree. The water barons intend to shatter the mechanism entirely, locking the seabed dry forever while they control the last stagnant cisterns above. Every page confirms that Gullmouth is meant to die of thirst while these high platforms hoard the remnant tide. A single iron-keyed corridor leads deeper into the stilt-city core past the patrols.

td-3-108.title: The Dusty Annex
td-3-108.text: Rotting charts and damp tidal logs carpet the floor of this forgotten alcove, where the air tastes of old paper and stagnant bilge. Intricate brass-faced locks hum faintly from every cabinet, guarding secrets that the water barons would rather leave to mould in the dark. Narrow grates in the floor vent the chill draught of the empty seabed far below, carrying the distant, hollow moans of the stilt-city struts. Every shadow seems to hold a watcher, and every surface invites a desperate pry or a stolen glance.

td-3-109.title: The Crumbling Ledger
td-3-109.text: Brittle pages flake away into grey dust at the lightest touch, bearing centuries of high-tide calculations and water-tax tallies. Eyes strain across fading iron-gall ink to trace the sequence of emergency overrides once used by the original Tidewardens. Acrid mould spores rise from the binding like yellow smoke, catching in the throat and setting off a silent, burning cough that threatens to draw the sentinels from the corridor. Only a few lines remain legible before the binding entirely disintegrates into the floor grates.

td-3-110.title: The Cipher in Ash
td-3-110.text:
Black spores cling to your eyelashes as you hunch over the rotting spine of the ledger, your fingers burning from the salt-acid eating the paper. Every breath draws more of the choking rot into your lungs, threatening to force a cough that would bring the Brineholder guards outside the alcove. Yet the faded ink of the final water-tax tally reveals the repeating numerical sequence of the vault tumbler, half-erased by damp. You steady your shaking hands against the wooden desk, squinting through streaming tears to catch the last crucial digit before the remaining text dissolves into grey sludge.

With your lungs locking up and the parchment crumbling into useless ash beneath your fingertips, you throw your weight against the hidden latch to test the sequence.

td-3-111.title: Choked on the Dust
td-3-111.text: A thick cloud of black spores bursts from the spine of the ancient ledger, catching the throat in a sudden, violent spasm. Coughing tears at the chest wall, leaving a metallic taste of blood and rotten linen on the tongue while the eyes stream with blinding tears. Footsteps halt in the outer passage at the sudden noise, forcing a frantic scramble into the shadows behind a stack of empty water casks. The secret numbers are lost to the dust, and the lungs will ache with every breath for hours to come.

td-3-112.title: The Vault Combination
td-3-112.text:
Your fingertips trace the fading, ash-grey digits pressed into the final intact margin before the parchment dissolves entirely into your damp palm. You cough against the black spores clinging to your tongue, memorizing the sequence of turns required for the heavy iron tumblers. Amidst the rot and the bitter taste of salt-acid, you secure the cipher that opens the Brineholder vaults.

It is a heavy copper tally-token stamped with the seal of the high water-tax office, heavy enough to crack a tooth and recognized by every gate-warden on the stilts.
exits: Slip away before the guards return
